subject: Deployment profile follow-up: isolation concerns & next steps
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Park <dpark@pulsecore.com>
Cc: Michael Lee <mlee@pulsecore.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment profile follow-up: isolation concerns & next steps

Hi Danielle / Michael —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the right deployment option (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC).

Call highlights:
- PulseCore is evaluating LLM-powered clinical triage for US patients; sensitive PHI in prompts.
- Primary concerns: noisy-neighbor risk, isolation boundaries for PHI, and latency SLOs for triage flows.
- Shortlist: Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private (VPC/on-prem) depending on compliance needs.

Requested items / clarification:
1) Expected production traffic (p50/p95 latency targets and peak qps). You mentioned a small pilot — can you confirm expected peak qps and token sizes?
2) Compliance: will you require a signed BAA and data residency limited to US regions only? Any additional regulatory controls?
3) Isolation tolerance: are you comfortable with Dedicated (isolated GPU pools + tenant-level controls) or do you need a Private VPC/on-prem separation for the pilot?
4) Fallback: do you want automatic fallback to Hosted in case of capacity constraints?

I attached a short risk comparison table (shared_vs_dedicated_risk_table.xlsx) and our SOC2 summary (redwood_soc2_summary.pdf) to help your security reviewers.

Proposed next steps:
- If you prefer, we can schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive (infra + security) Wed 9/22 or Thu 9/23.
- We’ll prepare a cost sensitivity table and a draft mutual action plan after we get the traffic and compliance answers above.

Thanks — simple replies to the numbered items above will help us move fast.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
attachments: shared_vs_dedicated_risk_table.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Danielle Park <dpark@pulsecore.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Lee <mlee@pulsecore.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment profile follow-up: isolation concerns & next steps

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A few answers below:

1) Traffic: for pilot we expect ~40–60 qps sustained with 120 qps peaks during business hours. Token sizes will be small (~120 tokens avg).
2) SLOs: target p50 <200ms, p95 <700ms. If p95 is >1s we’ll need mitigation plans.
3) Compliance: yes, we will require a BAA for handling PHI and all data must remain in US regions. Our compliance team will want SOC2 + encryption details.
4) Isolation preference: we prefer Dedicated reserved capacity for production pilot to minimize noisy-neighbor risk. For immediate go-live we are open to a hybrid: Dedicated primary with Hosted fallback for overflow if needed, provided fallback does not keep PHI in shared infrastructure.

Can you also provide a ballpark cost delta between Dedicated (reserved) vs Hosted for the pilot scale? That’ll help my finance partner.

Regards,
Danielle Park
Head of Product, PulseCore Technologies

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Deployment profile follow-up: isolation concerns & next steps (internal)

Aisha / Rishi —

Good detail from Danielle. Suggest we propose a hybrid pathway that meets both compliance and time-to-value:

Recommendation (high-level):
- Production pilot: Dedicated reserved capacity in US region (pin model version + KV cache disabled for non-PII flows).
- PHI handling: For PHI-containing prompts, offer Private VPC option (customer-managed networking) — same API surface but separate control plane.
- Overflow/fallback: Allow Hosted fallback for non-PHI overflow only; for PHI overflow route to Private/Dedicated queue.

Action items:
1) Send BAA + SOC2 + encryption summary to Danielle (BAA will go via DocuSign).
2) Prepare a cost sensitivity table (hosted vs dedicated reserved) for 60/120 qps scenarios — I’ll draft numbers.
3) Schedule a tech deep-dive with infra and security (30–45 min). Wed 9/23 10–11am PT or Thu 9/24 2–3pm PT — pick a slot that works for PulseCore.

Attaching a draft mutual action plan to get the procurement timeline started (mutual_action_plan_pulsecore.docx).

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
attachments: mutual_action_plan_pulsecore.docx
